title: Add rollout cohort dashboards and alert templates
author: Aisha Bello
description:
This PR adds a set of internal rollout cohort dashboards (Grafana) and alert templates (Prometheus rule groups + notification routing defaults) to support Hosted canary rollouts. The intent is to standardize the signals SRE/Oncall and product teams watch during a rollout, reduce time-to-diagnosis when the canary regresses, and provide sensible defaults for the auto-stop/rollback thresholds work. The dashboards are built around the new rollout_id + cohort tags (baseline/canary) and include guardrails to avoid high-cardinality views by default.

What’s included: (1) Grafana dashboards: A “Hosted Rollout Overview” dashboard (per tenant + route) that shows rollout state context (rollout_id, step %, regions) and top-line SLO signals side-by-side for baseline vs canary: request rate, 5xx rate, timeout rate, cancellation rate (streaming), and p50/p95/p99 latency. A “Cohort Comparison Deep Dive” dashboard with latency heatmaps by model + region, tokens/sec (where present), and a panel to compare deltas (canary - baseline) with a configurable lookback. A “Rollout Debug” dashboard focused on data-plane symptoms: routing decisions, cohort assignment distribution, retry rates, and mismatch indicators. All dashboards default to route + region filters and require explicit rollout_id selection for per-rollout drilldown.

(2) Alert templates: Adds alert rule groups intended for oncall and as building blocks for the rollout orchestrator auto-stop logic: ElevatedCanary5xxRate, ElevatedCanaryTimeoutRate, CanaryP95LatencyRegression (relative to baseline), and CanaryErrorBudgetBurn (short window) with recommended thresholds and evaluation windows aligned to minimum soak time. Alerts are written to be cohort-aware and to suppress noise when traffic is < N req/min (to reduce false positives in early steps like 1% and 5%). We also add a companion alert “RolloutCohortMetricsMissing” to catch telemetry gaps (e.g., rollout_id tag not present or aggregation pipeline lagging).

(3) Docs/runbook pointers embedded in dashboards: Each dashboard has a “What to do next” text panel linking to the internal runbook for stuck/bad split and to the hosted rollouts SLO metrics guidance so that oncall has a single place to start.

Cardinality / performance notes: dashboards intentionally avoid top-K by rollout_id across all tenants. The only global view is a rollup by route + region with optional drilldown. Where queries require rollout_id, they are gated behind a variable and are scoped to a single tenant. There is also a new recording rule to pre-aggregate cohort rates by (tenant_id, route_id, region, cohort) to keep dashboard queries fast.

Testing: Verified in staging with a seeded canary rollout (10% step) and validated panels render under 5s. Confirmed alert rules load and evaluate without missing series. Also validated that early-stage traffic (< 30 rpm) does not trigger latency regression alerts.

Rollout plan: Land behind internal enablement only; dashboards are not customer-visible. SRE can import the dashboards via the existing grafana-sync job. Alert rules are deployed with the standard prometheus-rules bundle and are disabled by default in prod until beta tuning is complete.

Follow-ups (not in scope): (a) Add a UI link from Console rollout page to the internal Grafana dashboard for employees (requires auth boundary work). (b) Quality-metric panels once we have standardized quality signals. (c) Dedicated/Private dashboard variants once cohort tags are enabled there.

Refs: ENG-9152 (telemetry tags + aggregation), ENG-9158 (auto-stop/rollback), PM-1859 (GA checklist - monitoring + runbooks).

obs: add cohort comparison deep dive dashboard + variables
prometheus: add cohort-aware recording rules for request/error/latency

review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: Love the direction. Two asks: (1) ensure alerts don’t fire at 1% when traffic is tiny, and (2) add an explicit panel for cohort split distribution (expected vs observed) because we’ve already seen mismatch issues in beta.

Aisha Bello (author): Added a traffic floor (req/min) to all regression alerts and documented it in the alert README. Also added a “Cohort distribution” panel to the Debug dashboard using the routing decision counter and the cohort tag, scoped to route+region.

Thomas Baird: Query cost looks OK for single-tenant drilldown, but the overview dashboard still has a variable that defaults to ‘All tenants’ and could be expensive. Can we hard-disable ‘All’ for tenant_id and require explicit selection?

Aisha Bello (author): Good catch. Updated dashboard variables: tenant_id is required (no ‘All’), and rollout_id is hidden until tenant_id is selected. Also moved some rate calcs to recording rules to reduce panel query complexity.

Allison Grant: Can we tighten the latency regression definition? Relative deltas can be noisy if baseline is already degraded. Suggest adding an absolute guard (e.g., canary p95 > X ms) OR use baseline+delta. Also please add a note about streaming vs non-streaming routes since p95 for streaming time-to-first-token is different.

Aisha Bello (author): Implemented baseline+delta style: canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * (1 + pct) and canary_p95 > absolute_ms. Added separate panels for TTFT vs end-to-end latency when the metric exists, and noted streaming caveats in the dashboard info panel.

Logan Wright: Looks aligned with the tagging work. One concern: recording rule labels include rollout_id in one rule group—can we drop rollout_id from recording rules to avoid cardinality issues and keep per-rollout drilldown on raw series only?

Aisha Bello (author): Agreed. Removed rollout_id from all recording rules. Per-rollout drilldown panels now query raw series filtered by rollout_id (scoped to tenant+route+region). Recording rules only cover (tenant_id, route_id, region, cohort).

Felix Schneider: Minor: Can we rename ‘baseline’/‘canary’ legend labels to match Console wording (‘Control’/‘Canary’)? Also the dashboard description mentions ‘tokens/sec’ but we don’t have that everywhere.
Aisha Bello (author): Updated legend aliases to Control/Canary. Adjusted tokens/sec panels to be conditional with a ‘not available for this route/model’ text when series are missing.
Sean Gallagher: Final pass looks good. Approved once the prod default for alerts is disabled and there’s a clear enablement note.
Aisha Bello (author): Added ‘disabled by default’ in the rule manifest and a comment with the enablement steps + owner (SRE) for beta tuning.
release_notes: Internal only: adds standard Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert templates for Hosted rollout cohort monitoring (baseline/control vs canary), including latency/error/timeout regressions with traffic floors and a metrics-missing alert to detect tagging/aggregation gaps.
